stories.headline: Sonata Software: EBITDA margin fell to 15.4% from 20.2% despite pipeline, order-win beats
stories.instagram_caption:
Sonata's AI pipeline rose 21% to $340M, and order wins were up 27% QoQ — ahead of May guidance.
EBITDA margin fell to 15.4%, down from 20.2% the prior period.
Management cited a one-time compensation reversal, AI investments, deal ramp delays, and a forex impact of ₹35.4 crore.
Utilization dipped to 88.5%.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: SONATA SOFTWARE — Q1 FY27]
Sonata's AI pipeline grew 21% to $340 million, and order wins rose 27% quarter-on-quarter — both ahead of May's guidance.
[ON-SCREEN: EBITDA margin: 20.2% → 15.4%]
But EBITDA margin fell sharply, from 20.2% in the prior period to 15.4% this quarter.
[ON-SCREEN: Cited: one-time comp reversal, AI investment, ramp delays, forex hit ₹35.4 Cr]
Management attributed the drop to a one-time compensation reversal, higher AI investment, delayed deal ramp-ups, and a forex impact of ₹35.4 crore.
[ON-SCREEN: Utilization: 88.5%]
Utilization dipped to 88.5%, with recovery expected next quarter.

stories.headline: Jain Irrigation cuts FY27 margin guidance to 14% from February's 18-20%, after Q1 PAT fell 90%
stories.instagram_caption:
Jain Irrigation had guided 18-20% FY27 standalone margins back in February.
That guidance is now revised down to 14%.
Q1 revenue fell 2.5% YoY to ₹1,500 crore; adjusted PAT fell to ₹3 crore from ₹30 crore a year earlier.
Management attributes the shortfall to monsoon delays and a 50% polymer price hike, and expects a second-half recovery.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
stories.youtube_shorts_script:
[ON-SCREEN: JAIN IRRIGATION — Q1 FY27]
Back in February, Jain Irrigation guided FY27 standalone margins of 18 to 20 percent.
[ON-SCREEN: Guidance: 18-20% → 14%]
That guidance has now been revised down to 14 percent.
[ON-SCREEN: Revenue: -2.5% YoY | PAT: ₹3 Cr vs ₹30 Cr]
Q1 revenue fell 2.5% year-on-year to ₹1,500 crore, and adjusted profit after tax dropped to ₹3 crore, down from ₹30 crore a year earlier.
[ON-SCREEN: Cited: monsoon delays, 50% polymer price hike]
Management cited monsoon delays and a 50% jump in polymer prices, which pushed customer orders into later quarters.
[ON-SCREEN: Double-digit FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained]
Double-digit full-year revenue growth guidance was maintained, with management expecting recovery in the second half.
[ON-SCREEN: Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.]

stories.headline: Rajshree Polypack raises plastics guidance to ₹420-430cr; quietly cuts Olive JV guidance to ~₹90cr
stories.instagram_caption:
Rajshree Polypack's core plastics packaging guidance for FY27 was raised to ₹420-430 crore.
In the same call, guidance for its Olive JV was cut to about ₹90 crore, down from the earlier ₹120-130 crore.
Q1 results: revenue ₹102.91 crore (+24.7% YoY), EBITDA margin 16.05%.
The JV guidance cut sits within an overall upgraded outlook.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.

[ON-SCREEN: Olive JV guidance: ₹120-130 Cr → ~₹90 Cr]

stories.headline: Great Eastern Shipping again declines guidance despite its most profitable quarter ever
stories.instagram_caption:
Great Eastern Shipping's management again declined to give earnings guidance on this call.
That's despite delivering its most profitable quarter ever: consolidated profit of ₹1,309 crore.
MR tankers were earning near $50,000/day; LPG carriers above $100,000/day — both near all-time highs.
Order book stands at 27% for crude tankers and 35% for LPG.
Factual summary of public company disclosures. Not investment advice.
